title: Functors preserving sums and generators preserve the localizing closures
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal T'$ be triangulated categories with arbitrary direct sums, $\mathcal G\subset\mathcal T$ and
$\mathcal G'\subset\mathcal T'$ full subcategories, and $F\colon\mathcal T\to\mathcal T'$ an exact functor preserving
direct sums with $F(\mathcal G)\subset\Loc(\mathcal G')$. Then $F(\Loc(\mathcal G))\subset\Loc(\mathcal G')$, and the
restriction $\Loc(\mathcal G)\to\Loc(\mathcal G')$ is exact and preserves direct sums. In particular this applies
with $\mathcal T=\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, $\mathcal G=\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ ([sk-def-localizing-closure]).

Here triangulated categories and exact functors have the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. All direct sums are indexed by sets in a fixed indexing universe. For any class of objects $\mathcal H$ of such a category $\mathcal C$, $\Loc(\mathcal H)$ denotes the full subcategory on the objects belonging to every full replete triangulated subcategory of $\mathcal C$ containing $\mathcal H$ and closed under these ambient sums. Replete means closed under isomorphisms; the triangulated structure on a full triangulated subcategory is induced from its ambient category [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. In the final specialization the coefficient and derived-category conventions are precisely those of [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text: Unpack the intersection defining $\Loc(\mathcal H)$. The ambient category is a candidate. Every candidate contains $\mathcal H$ and zero, is replete, is stable under every integer shift, and has the distinguished-triangle closure condition of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Each of these conditions is preserved by intersection of object predicates: an object, a shifted object, or a required vertex of a distinguished triangle lies in every candidate as soon as the given vertices do. The same argument applies to a small ambient coproduct of objects in every candidate. Thus the intersection is itself a full replete triangulated subcategory closed under small sums, and is contained in every candidate. This proves the closure properties and minimality used below, for arbitrary $\mathcal H$, without a smallness assumption on the class of candidates.

source.place: first paragraph, unpacking the definition before the minimality inference; full triangulated subcategories: Stacks Tag 05QM and Tag 05QX

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=\Loc(\mathcal G)$ and $\mathcal L'=\Loc(\mathcal G')$, and let $\mathcal S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal T$ on $K\in\mathcal L$ with $F(K)\in\mathcal L'$. The hypothesis puts every object of $\mathcal G$ in $\mathcal S$. Exactness means that $F$ is additive, commutes with shifts, and maps distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. In particular $F(0)\simeq0$, so zero lies in $\mathcal S$; $F(K[n])\simeq F(K)[n]$ shows shift closure. If $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ is distinguished and $K,M\in\mathcal S$, $K,M\in\mathcal L$ imply $L\in\mathcal L$ by triangle closure; its image is distinguished, and $F(K),F(M)\in\mathcal L'$ force $F(L)\in\mathcal L'$. Thus $L\in\mathcal S$, which is the full triangulated-subcategory criterion [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. An isomorphism $K\simeq L$ induces $F(K)\simeq F(L)$, proving repleteness. For any small family $K_i\in\mathcal S$, its sum belongs to $\mathcal L$ and $F(\bigoplus_iK_i)\simeq\bigoplus_iF(K_i)$ belongs to $\mathcal L'$; hence its sum lies in $\mathcal S$. Thus $\mathcal S$ is a localizing candidate containing $\mathcal G$. Minimality from step 1 gives $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal S$, proving $F(\mathcal L)\subseteq\mathcal L'$.

source.place: first paragraph, subcategory S, closure checks and minimality; exactness: Stacks Tag 014V, triangulated-subcategory criterion: Tags 05QM and 05QX

proof.text: Restrict $F$ on objects and morphisms using step 2; fullness makes its identity and composition laws the ambient laws. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] both localizing subcategories carry the ambient shifts and precisely the ambient distinguished triangles whose vertices lie in them. The shift isomorphism of $F$ restricts because both subcategories are shift-stable. Every distinguished triangle in $\mathcal L$ is ambient distinguished, so its $F$-image is ambient distinguished by [def-weil-triangulated-category] and has all vertices in $\mathcal L'$ by step 2. It is therefore distinguished in $\mathcal L'$. The restricted functor is exact.

source.place: second paragraph, exactness of the restriction; Stacks Tags 014V and 05QX

proof.text: For a small family $K_i\in\mathcal L$, let $K=\bigoplus_iK_i$ be the ambient coproduct, which lies in $\mathcal L$ by step 1. For every $A\in\mathcal L$, fullness identifies the coproduct universal-property map with the ambient bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K,A)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(K_i,A)$, so the same coprojections exhibit $K$ as a coproduct in $\mathcal L$. The identical argument holds in $\mathcal L'$. Since $F$ preserves ambient coproduct cocones, its restricted functor therefore preserves these coproducts. For the empty family this argument says that the ambient zero is still initial in the full subcategory, so it covers empty sums too.

source.place: second paragraph, ambient direct sums; universal property written out

proof.text: For the final example use exactly the ambient module-object derived category and $\Dctf$ specified in [sk-def-localizing-closure], not a category of derived-complete objects. It is an unbounded derived category under that convention, and has all small direct sums by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] (1). Its closure of $\Dctf$ is the same full replete coproduct-closed triangulated intersection by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Thus steps 1--4 apply with this $\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal G$, whenever $F$ satisfies the stated hypotheses. No particular functor, geometric preservation theorem, or additional conclusion about coefficients is asserted.
